# Capability inventory — what the repository actually contains

**Date:** 30 October 2026
**Method:** generated by reading the repository at `integration@0c124e5`; every claim links to
files in this checkout. Reproduction commands are at the end. This is the 1–3 Nov deliverable
of the [14-day plan](POST_HACKATHON_ROADMAP.md#16-immediate-14-day-plan-114-november-2026):
classify actual code, interfaces, storage, tests and deployments as
**Implemented / Partial / Absent / Unknown**, starting from the [repository check](POST_HACKATHON_ROADMAP.md#repository-check-30-october-2026).

Statuses here describe the code as it exists today. They do not assert release readiness; the
[acceptance gates](POST_HACKATHON_ROADMAP.md#13-acceptance-gates) decide that.

## 2. Memory core

**Status: Implemented; the record contract (revision, actor, proposed) closed
2026-10-30 — export/import remains the named gap.**

- **Record schema** ([memory.ts](../../packages/shared/src/memory.ts)): ten memory types
  (`preference`, `project`, `technical_decision`, `constraint`, `verified_solution`,
  `failed_approach`, `unfinished_task`, `goal`, `correction`, `contextual_fact`); two scopes
  (`global`, `project`); validation statuses (`unverified`, `verified`, `disputed`); lifecycle
  statuses (`active`, `superseded`, `deleted`, `expired`); provenance (`session_id`,
  `reference`, nullable but always present); `supersedes[]` / `superseded_by` edges; tags;
  content capped at 8,000 chars; `expires_at` for retention.
- **Confidence** is `z.number().min(0).max(1)` — uncalibrated. The roadmap rule (treat as
  metadata, not probability, until calibrated) holds; relabelling the schema comment is a G1 item.
- **Retrieval** ([retrieval.ts](../../packages/memory-engine/src/retrieval.ts),
  [fts.ts](../../packages/memory-engine/src/fts.ts)): SQLite FTS5 with porter stemming
  (migration 4), progressive relaxation and recency fallback, token budgets, content-hash
  dedupe ([content-hash.ts](../../packages/memory-engine/src/content-hash.ts)).
  Measured by `pnpm eval:retrieval` and `pnpm bench:retrieval`.
- **Correction/supersession**: one transaction with supersession edges and history;
  API at `POST /api/memories/:id/correct` ([memories.ts](../../apps/server/src/routes/memories.ts));
  history at `GET /api/memories/:id/history`. `superseded` is auditable history, never a
  current fact (comment in [memory.ts](../../packages/shared/src/memory.ts)).
- **Capture** ([memory-capture.ts](../../packages/agent-core/src/memory-capture.ts)):
  explicit "remember …", correction detection, deterministic supersession targeting, and
  candidate proposals that require user confirmation before saving.
- **Record contract (closed 2026-10-30, migration v7 / D038):** records carry
  `revision` (monotonic; every in-place change bumps it; `PATCH` supports
  `expected_revision` with a 409 conflict) and a record-level `actor`
  (mirrors the latest `MemoryHistoryEntry.actor`: `user|agent|system`);
  `proposed` is a lifecycle state decided by accept/reject endpoints and kept
  out of retrieval.
- **Export/import (closed 2026-10-30, D039):** `GET /api/memories/export` and
  `POST /api/memories/import` move a versioned envelope covering tombstones,
  audit history and supersession edges; imports are atomic, idempotent on
  replay, refuse newer formats and support `dry_run`.

## 3. Integration layer

**Status: Implemented (for this phase). A REST API, six bounded tools, a versioned shared
tool contract, and an MCP (stdio) surface over the SAME registry exist. List traversal is
uniform (`limit`/`offset` + filter-wide `total` on memories, review queue, and sessions —
the sessions `total` was fixed from page-length to a real COUNT, 2026-10-30), and errors are
machine-readable via a versioned catalogue (`GET /api/errors`, `catalog_version: 1`, mirrored
in `/api/meta.errors`; tests compare live responses against published entries, so mapping
drift fails CI — D048). `Idempotency-Key` replay (24h window, SQLite-backed, first-wins)
covers `POST /api/memories` and Forge generation — D049; §3's named remainders are closed.**

- **HTTP API** (Fastify; routes in [app.ts](../../apps/server/src/app.ts) and
  [routes/](../../apps/server/src/routes)):
  - Sessions: `POST/GET /api/sessions`, `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/sessions/:id`,
    `GET /api/sessions/:id/messages/:messageId`, `POST /api/sessions/:id/messages` (SSE turn).
  - Memories/projects: `GET /api/projects`, `GET /api/memories` (filtered list),
    `GET/POST /api/memories`, `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/memories/:id`,
    `POST /api/memories/:id/correct`, `GET /api/memories/:id/history`,
    `GET /api/memories/stats`, `POST /api/retrieval/preview`.
  - Tools: `GET /api/tools`, `GET /api/sessions/:id/tools`,
    `POST /api/sessions/:id/tools/:callId/decision`.
  - Generated UI: `GET/POST /api/sessions/:id/ui`,
    `POST /api/sessions/:id/ui/:surfaceId/events`.
  - Forge (HTML Studio): project CRUD, `generate`, `jobs/:jobId` + `cancel`/`diff`/`approve`/
    `reject`, `rollback`, `artifact`, `preview`, `recovery/ack`, `storage-check`
    ([routes/forge.ts](../../apps/server/src/routes/forge.ts)).
  - Ops: `GET /api/health`, `POST /api/health/muse`, `GET /api/live`, `GET /api/meta`,
    `POST /api/provider/generate`.
- **Six tools** ([tools.ts](../../packages/tool-runtime/src/tools.ts)) with declared
  side-effect class: `memory.search` (read), `memory.create` (write), `project.get` (read),
  `project.update` (write), `task.create` (write), `task.list` (read). Registry enforces
  Zod validation and confirmation for writes ([registry.ts](../../packages/tool-runtime/src/registry.ts)).
- **Muse CLI provider** ([muse-cli-provider.ts](../../packages/muse-provider/src/muse-cli-provider.ts)):
  stateless `muse exec --json` adapter; verified behaviour in
  [muse-integration.md](../muse-integration.md). An `echo-provider.ts` exists for offline/Codespaces use.
- **MCP surface** ([packages/mcp-server](../../packages/mcp-server/src/index.ts), stdio entry
  [main.ts](../../packages/mcp-server/src/main.ts), `pnpm mcp:serve`): the same six tools over
  the Model Context Protocol from the same `createDefaultToolRegistry()`; JSON Schemas (input
  AND output) derived from the tools' zod contracts so clients can validate structured results;
  project scope and the writes policy are startup-bound, never model-supplied; a
  `mcp-recall://contract` resource publishes the version, scope, and write policy.
- **Versioned contract** (`TOOL_CONTRACT_VERSION` in [shared/tool.ts](../../packages/shared/src/tool.ts)):
  stamped into `GET /api/tools` and the MCP contract resource; conformance tests pin MCP tool
  list ≡ registry list ([mcp-contract.test.ts](../../tests/integration/mcp-contract.test.ts))
  and the REST stamping ([tools-contract.test.ts](../../tests/integration/tools-contract.test.ts)).
- **Absent:** MCP client usage in-product. Sessions turns deliberately rely on the
  `session_busy` lock rather than idempotency keys; proposals on content dedup (D049).

## 4. Trust boundary

**Status: Partial. Structural guards, approval/audit, and (since 2026-10-30) an optional shared-token authentication layer exist; identity and per-project authorization do not.**

- **Loopback-only by default**: non-loopback bind refused at startup; Host-header validation
  blocks DNS rebinding ([host-guard.ts](../../apps/server/src/host-guard.ts)); origin guard for
  browser clients ([origin-guard.ts](../../apps/server/src/origin-guard.ts)) with CI test
  [forge-origin-guard.test.ts](../../tests/integration/forge-origin-guard.test.ts).
- **Optional shared bearer token** (2026-10-30, gap G-6 groundwork, D045):
  `ACCESS_TOKEN` gates every `/api` route (liveness excepted) with a timing-safe Bearer check
  that runs before the origin guard; enables a deliberate off-loopback bind (startup re-check
  warns instead of refusing); `/api/meta` states the posture (`loopback-only` | `shared-token`);
  web client sends it from `localStorage`. Tests: [access-token-auth.test.ts](../../tests/integration/access-token-auth.test.ts).
- **Approval is two-phase** (D032 in [DECISIONS.md](../DECISIONS.md)): write tool calls
  persist as `pending`; `POST /api/sessions/:id/tools/:callId/decision` approves or denies.
  Forge approvals bind to an exact-byte SHA-256 and refuse stale bases (CAS) — see
  [forge-api.test.ts](../../tests/integration/forge-api.test.ts) ("refuses a stale approval
  after another change lands", "serialises concurrent approvals").
- **Project scope comes from the session, never the model** (D033): no tool accepts a
  project id argument; cross-project access is structurally impossible.
- **Audit is append-only and records failures**: statuses
  `pending|executed|failed|denied|invalid` ([store.ts](../../packages/tool-runtime/src/store.ts), D034).
- **Decision Guard is advisory by design** ([decision-guard/src/index.ts](../../packages/decision-guard/src/index.ts),
  integration in [forge/decision-guard.ts](../../apps/server/src/forge/decision-guard.ts)):
  seven rule families over decisions (A–G, engine v1.5.0; G-7 added autoplay-media and
  external-assets); advisories recorded but
  a human can proceed ("advisory-blocked-but-approved" in
  [forge-decision-guard.test.ts](../../tests/integration/forge-decision-guard.test.ts)).
- **Absent:** identity (the token authenticates without identifying), per-project
  authorization for remote clients, quotas, credential lifecycle (rotation/expiry), and the
  adversarial suite that roadmap §5 makes a release criterion. The threat model in
  [security.md](../security.md) (T1–T10) covers the local-beta case; token mode documents its
  own residual risks in that file.

## 5. Application layer

**Status: Implemented for the local product (explorer = the Memory surface; its review
queue landed 2026-10-30, gap G-9 Partial); relationship graph/timeline views remain absent.**

- **Four surfaces** ([views.ts](../../apps/web/src/views.ts)): HTML Studio (`studio`),
  Memory (`memories`), Conversations (`conversations`), System (`system`). Component groups:
  [components/forge/](../../apps/web/src/components/forge),
  [components/memory/](../../apps/web/src/components/memory),
  [components/conversations/](../../apps/web/src/components/conversations),
  [components/studio/](../../apps/web/src/components/studio) — memory inspector with
  provenance/correction history, tool activity panel with Approve/Deny, generated-surface
  rendering, Forge diff/approval/rollback and recovery banners.
- **Generated UI protocol** ([schema.ts](../../packages/ui-protocol/src/schema.ts)): closed
  declarative block set — `heading`, `text`, `status`, `progress`, `tasklist`, `table`,
  `card`, `button`, `form` — with a validator ([validate.ts](../../packages/ui-protocol/src/validate.ts));
  no markup or script in the protocol.
- **Review queue** (2026-10-30, roadmap §7 first slice, D044): a derived panel in the
  Memory surface listing memories that need a human decision — unverified, disputed,
  past expiry, or expiring within a per-request horizon. `GET /api/memories/review`
  ([routes/memories.ts](../../apps/server/src/routes/memories.ts)) over
  [engine.reviewQueue](../../packages/memory-engine/src/engine.ts); triage is an ordinary
  PATCH (optimistic revision), so every decision lands in the append-only audit trail.
  Nothing is stored as a queue — membership is computed per request, so it cannot drift.
- **Absent:** relationship graph, timeline view, keyboard-nav audit for dense projects;
  a dedicated explorer surface separate from the Memory inspector.

## 6. Storage & persistence

**Status: Implemented; both named gaps (state_corrupt repair flow; fsync
durability) closed 2026-10-30.**

- **Eight migrations** ([migrations.ts](../../packages/memory-engine/src/migrations.ts)):
  v1 `core_memory_schema`, v2 `supersession_pointer_and_retrieval_indexes`,
  v3 `sessions_messages_and_turn_evidence`, v4 `porter_stemming_for_keyword_retrieval`,
  v5 `ui_surfaces_and_events`, v6 `project_tasks_and_tool_audit`,
  v7 `record_contract_revision_actor_proposed`, v8 `idempotency_keys` (transient replay
  records; excluded from the export envelope by design — D049). Forward-only;
  `db:migrate` reports schema version ([scripts/migrate.ts](../../apps/server/src/scripts/migrate.ts)).
- **Backup/purge/restore**: [backup.ts](../../apps/server/src/backup.ts) + `db:backup`, `db:restore`,
  `db:purge` ([scripts/db-backup.ts](../../apps/server/src/scripts/db-backup.ts),
  [scripts/db-restore.ts](../../apps/server/src/scripts/db-restore.ts),
  [scripts/purge.ts](../../apps/server/src/scripts/purge.ts)). Restores are integrity-checked and land
  only in an operator-named isolated target (`--into`; `--force` for deliberate replacement).
  The roadmap §8 drill is a standing gate: `pnpm backup:drill` seeds → backs up → destroys →
  restores → verifies record parity and the clobber guard, and CI runs it on every push (that IS
  the repo-side schedule; operators additionally cron it for live data). Drill timings are for a
  single local file and are explicitly NOT evidence for the hosted ≤4h recovery-time target.
- **Forge state**: `state.json` + `versions/` staging under
  [forge/workspace.ts](../../apps/server/src/forge/workspace.ts). A corrupt or missing
  `state.json` yields `state_corrupt` refusal — and since 2026-10-30 (PRs #32/#33)
  a guided flow exists: `recovery/state` inspection + `recovery/repair` archiving the
  damaged bytes and rebuilding from surviving versions, surfaced as a Studio banner
  (gap G-1 closed).
- **Job persistence** is atomic-rename based ([forge/job-store.ts](../../apps/server/src/forge/job-store.ts))
  plus fsync-before-rename since 2026-10-30 (PR #35, gap G-8 closed). Recovery integration tests exist
  ([forge-recovery.test.ts](../../tests/integration/forge-recovery.test.ts),
  [forge-completion-failure.test.ts](../../tests/integration/forge-completion-failure.test.ts)).
- **Runbooks (roadmap §8)**: [ops/OPERATOR_RUNBOOKS.md](../ops/OPERATOR_RUNBOOKS.md) —
  upgrade (backup-first, migration rehearsal on a copy), rollback (app-only; schema is
  forward-only by policy), incident triage (health/meta/errors/recovery endpoints, audit),
  and DR (backup cron example, isolated-then-forced restore, drill). Named accountable
  operator: the maintainer until a hosted deployment assigns one. **Alerts remain unmet**
  (roadmap G4 gate); the runbook lists the signals to wire them to rather than pretending.

## 7. Tests & verification

**Status: Implemented.**

- **Unit/integration/evaluation/research suites**: 47 test files — 27 unit, 14 integration
  (API, Forge lifecycle, recovery, origin guards, Codespaces), 5 evaluation (decision-guard
  accuracy corpus, forge-memory), 1 research (Phase 17 evidence).
- **Recorded baseline (this checkout, `integration@0c124e5`):** `pnpm verify` green —
  **739 passed, 3 skipped (742)**; the 3 skips are the live-Muse tests gated by
  `MML_LIVE_MUSE=1` ([muse-live.test.ts](../../tests/integration/muse-live.test.ts)).
  Duration ≈ 13 s; lint + typecheck precede the test run in the `verify` script.
  **Updated baseline (2026-10-30, after G-1/G-3/G-4/G-5/G-6-token/G-8/G-9-queue/G-11/G-12): 65 files,
  **866 passed, 3 skipped (869)**; the browser workflow now runs 46 checks
  across two engines (managed Chromium and managed Firefox), including per-engine
  visual snapshot comparison against committed baselines (tests/visual).
- **CI gates** ([ci.yml](../../.github/workflows/ci.yml)): "Lint, typecheck, test, build"
  and "Managed browser workflow (fake provider)" (Playwright Chromium) are *required
  status checks* on `integration` via the "Protect integration" ruleset; a second
  matrix leg "Managed browser workflow (fake provider · managed Firefox)" runs the
  same 44-check workflow on Firefox (roadmap §7, G-10).
- **Local Firefox caveat (macOS 27):** managed Firefox cannot launch on this host with
  Playwright 1.64.1 — the bundled build trips macOS TCC on the Firefox app-data dir
  (upstream [playwright#42768](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/42768),
  fixed upstream in a 1.65 roll). CI's Ubuntu runners are unaffected; the launcher
  policy is covered locally by [script-browser-policy.test.ts](../../tests/unit/script-browser-policy.test.ts).
- **Evidence/verify script families** ([package.json](../../package.json)):
  `verify:browser`, `verify:forge`, `verify:runtime`, `verify:security`,
  `verify:formsandbox`, `verify:studio-workflow`, `verify:research{,16,17}`,
  `eval:{retrieval,comparison,guard}`, `bench:{context,retrieval,muse-overhead}`,
  `demo:{sessions,tools,showcase,seed}`, `evidence:*`.

## 8. Deployments & entry points

**Status: Partial by design — judge-facing entry points are the public repo, Pages site, and Codespaces; there is no hosted app.**

- **Pages site** built from `main` by [website.yml](../../.github/workflows/website.yml)
  (workflow_dispatch; `deploy-ready` discipline noted in the site README).
- **Codespaces** ([.devcontainer](../../.devcontainer/devcontainer.json), `setup.sh`,
  [codespaces.ts](../../apps/server/src/codespaces.ts)) runs the app with the offline
  `echo` provider and a seeded demo.
- **The app itself** is single-user, loopback-only, no auth (§4). A hosted deployment is
  gated behind G4 in the roadmap; environment separation (staging/preview credentials)
  is not yet set up because there is nothing hosted.

## 11. Reproduction

```sh
# structure
find . -path ./node_modules -prune -o -name "*.test.ts*" -print   # 54 files
pnpm run verify                                                    # 866 pass / 3 skip
# retrieval & eval baselines
pnpm eval:retrieval        # 22-question corpus (2 misses documented)
pnpm bench:retrieval
# API surface
grep -nE "\.(get|post|patch|delete)\(" apps/server/src/routes/*.ts apps/server/src/app.ts
# tools & side effects
grep -n "id: '" packages/tool-runtime/src/tools.ts
# storage versions
grep -n "version:" packages/memory-engine/src/migrations.ts
# governance
gh api repos/sidonsoft/muse-recall/rulesets --jq '.[].name'        # 3 active rulesets
gh api repos/sidonsoft/muse-recall/private-vulnerability-reporting # {"enabled": true}
```

**Known discrepancies found while inventorying:**
1. The "Protect integration" ruleset, required status checks, and private vulnerability
   reporting are **already active** — roadmap §16's 1–3 Nov governance actions
   ("apply the prepared rulesets; enable private vulnerability reporting") are complete;
   update §16 and the G0 checklist when recording submission SHAs.
2. Retention **is** enforced, just not on a timer: `engine.expireStale()` runs at server
   startup ([index.ts:29–33](../../apps/server/src/index.ts)) and retrieval hard-filters
   `expires_at > now` in SQL ([retrieval.ts:379–380](../../packages/memory-engine/src/retrieval.ts)),
   so an expired memory is never served. Only the *status label* lags on a long-running
   server until the next restart — cosmetic for stats, not a correctness gap.
